topics.topic: Allowed characters and byte serialization for credentials and required headers
questions: Which code points count as control characters in a credential value?
How are valid non-ASCII credential values serialized on the HTTP wire, and which definition of control character is used?
What byte encoding is used for non-ASCII required header values, or are such values invalid?
What exact set counts as a control character in credential and required-header values: ASCII C0 only, C0 plus DEL, C0/C1, or Unicode general category `Cc`?

judgement.why: This is the same question about credential and required-header character rules and wire encoding already judged in P46, and the relevant latest texts have not changed since that judgement.

precedent.topic: Credential and required-header decoding, wire encoding, character rules, and size limits
precedent.why: Credential stripping, character sets, wire encoding and field-size constraints are encoding, format and field-contract details belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Creation, ownership, and permission requirements for the private data directory and its contents
questions: What exact ownership and permission checks define “private,” and are parent directories, SQLite side files and newly created files included?
Which owners, group memberships, permission bits and ACLs make the data directory or one of its contents unacceptable?
Must the data directory already exist, and what ownership and permission bits exactly satisfy “private”; may the kernel create an absent directory securely?

judgement.why: This is the same question about the meaning of a private data directory already judged in P7, and the quoted privacy passage remains unchanged.

precedent.topic: Exact ownership and permission requirements for a private data directory
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Exact release dependency set and whether bubblewrap is version-pinned
questions: Must the release pin and verify an exact `bubblewrap` version, or may any host version that passes the probe serve as the security boundary?
What exact dependency set and versions constitute release v1?
What are the complete dependency names and exact versions for release v1, including the sandbox runtime and `bubblewrap` if it is covered?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list.
judgement.why: The complete dependency set and whether bubblewrap belongs to the pinned sandbox runtime were already unspecified by this unchanged passage, and the change did not make that choice newly material.

topics.topic: Filesystem access boundaries for function code and the exchange directory
questions: May function code read arbitrary files in the read-only runtime and read or write arbitrary paths in the exchange directory, or may it access only its declared input and output artifacts?
May agent code create, enumerate and read arbitrary files inside the exchange directory, or may it access only runner-provided input and output locations?
May function code inspect arbitrary runtime files and create or read arbitrary exchange-directory files, or must access be limited to runner-managed input and output objects?

judgement.why: This is the same sandbox-filesystem-boundary question already judged in P23, and the relevant passage was not changed.

quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when a valid HTTP status is followed by an oversized, incomplete, or failed body
questions: Does an oversized 3xx, 4xx or 5xx response keep its status-derived outcome after the body is truncated, or does exceeding `service_response_bytes_max` produce a distinct failure?

If valid final status and headers arrive but the body times out, resets or ends prematurely, is that “no valid final response” and therefore unknown, or a status-derived applied/not-applied outcome with invalid outputs?
At what point is a final response valid enough for the status row to take precedence over a later transport or body failure?

If valid 2xx status and headers arrive but the body then times out, resets, ends before its declared length, or has malformed transfer framing, is a non-read attempt `unknown` or `applied` with `contract_violation`?

judgement.why: This is the same question about transport deadline coverage and incomplete-response classification already decided by the later contract in P9.

precedent.topic: Transport deadline coverage and classification of incomplete response bodies
quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] One deadline from monotonic_deadline with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS constant covers connecting, writing and reading the whole response; the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, a longer body being over the ceiling.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.
precedent.why: The later transport contract applies one deadline through the complete response and classifies timeout, reset or end-of-stream before status-class outcomes.

topics.topic: Permitted api_base_url components and exact final URL and Host-header construction
questions: Are user-info, a query, a fragment, or a non-root path allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path and represented in the Host header?
Which `api_base_url` components are permitted, and how are a base path, query, fragment, userinfo, IPv6 host and explicit port represented in the final URL and Host header?
How are semantically equivalent but textually unusual authorities handled, including case, default ports, IPv6 brackets and percent-encoding, so the described Host header is exactly the wire header?
May `api_base_url` contain userinfo, a query, fragment, or a path prefix, and does removing a trailing slash remove one slash or all trailing slashes?

judgement.why: This is the same api_base_url grammar, URL joining and Host serialization question already assigned to State 6 in P2.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and deterministic URL joining
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Representation, identity, and class of an empty mapped many-file output
questions: How does a NodeExecution represent and type an empty `many` file output when there are no SpooledFile facts and M23 permits only StoredValue or SpooledFile references?
How does that NodeExecution represent an empty `many` file output and its disclosure class?

Where is the aggregate class and ordered-list identity of a mapped `many` file output represented, especially when the list is empty, given that M23 can name only individual SpooledFile facts and run files cannot be StoredValues?

judgement.why: This is the same question about the representation and disclosure class of mapped many-file outputs, including empty lists, already answered by the later contract in P51.

precedent.topic: Representation and disclosure class of many-file outputs, including empty lists
quotes: advance_run: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change; when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is; only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing; a mapped node's file output is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, since no record of its own holds it, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input; a mapped element receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class, or the spooled file at that position.
precedent.why: The later run contract represents a many-file output as an ordered SpooledFilesRef with its own disclosure class and explicitly assigns an empty list the highest class among the node's inputs.

topics.topic: Scope of prohibited clock and time observations in function sandboxes
questions: Are other CPython 3.12 clock-reading entry points, such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.clock_gettime_ns`, `time.thread_time`, `time.thread_time_ns` and `os.times`, allowed or sandbox violations?
May function code observe file timestamps or other time-bearing filesystem metadata?
Are omitted standard-library clock and timing APIs usable, or must all clock and elapsed-time observations be trapped despite not being in the closed list?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The treatment of clock and timing APIs omitted from the closed trap list was already left unresolved by this unchanged passage, and the change did not make it matter.

topics.topic: Validation or escaping of port names used as multipart field names
questions: What happens when a port name contains a quote, backslash, CR, LF, non-ASCII text or another character requiring Content-Disposition escaping?
How are quotes, backslashes, CR/LF, non-ASCII characters and other header-significant characters in port names handled?
Are quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters in port names refused or escaped, and by which exact encoding rule?

judgement.why: This is the same multipart field-name and filename escaping question already assigned to State 6 or later in P8.

precedent.topic: Safe encoding or rejection of multipart field names and filenames
precedent.why: Multipart header escaping, media-type grammar, boundary generation and wire framing are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Classification and precedence of malformed manifest structures and idempotency_key fields
questions: Which manifest-mismatch reason and precedence apply when fields are present with the wrong JSON type, capability entries are not objects, names are missing or non-strings, or canonicalization is impossible because of duplicate object keys?
What happens when the capability entry omits `idempotency_key`, or supplies a non-null non-string value?

How are syntactically valid but wrongly typed or incomplete manifest structures classified and ordered—for example non-array `capabilities`, non-object entries, missing or non-string names, absent `idempotency_key`, or a non-string key on a read operation?

judgement.why: This is the same complete-manifest-schema and malformed-member-classification question already assigned to State 6 in P4.

precedent.topic: Complete manifest schema and classification of malformed members
precedent.why: Complete manifest shapes, member types, duplicate-key handling and malformed-field precedence are schema and contract matters for State 6.

topics.topic: Deterministic collision-free multipart boundary selection
questions: How must the kernel choose or retry a multipart boundary when the chosen delimiter occurs in a part's bytes?
How is a boundary selected so the body is valid, deterministic enough for retry behavior, and collision-free with all parts?

judgement.why: This is the same multipart boundary generation and collision-handling question already assigned to State 6 or later in P14.

precedent.topic: Multipart boundary generation and collision handling
precedent.why: Multipart boundary generation, delimiter collision avoidance and wire framing are encoding and format decisions for State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Disclosure class of empty mapped operation outputs
questions: What class does an empty output list of a mapped operation node carry?
For an operation node mapped over an empty list, does each empty output list take the binding output port's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?

quotes:
At run time a value's class is set by the one rule of M21: a flow input takes
   its port's class, a constant its declared class, a function output the highest
   class its execution actually received, a binding output the class the binding
   declares, a trial case's input its contract input port's class and its
   expected output the highest class of the case's inputs.

an empty list
   takes the highest class among the node's inputs — the list it mapped over
   and every other input — as an execution of the node would have received
   them (M21), so no class is lowered;
judgement.why: The first passage assigns every binding output its binding-declared class, while the second assigns every empty mapped output list the highest class among the node's inputs.

topics.topic: Enforcement of deterministic function execution against untrapped nondeterminism
questions: How is this guarantee enforced for Python code that can observe process identity, object addresses, thread scheduling, filesystem enumeration or other nondeterministic state not covered by the listed traps?

How does the kernel prevent or classify other nondeterministic observations available through CPython, such as process IDs, object-address representations, filesystem metadata, locale or runtime scheduling?

judgement.why: This is the same question about enforcing deterministic execution against untrapped observations already judged in P34, and the relevant requirement remains unchanged.

precedent.topic: Required response to nondeterministic function execution
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Equality semantics for JSON guard values
questions: What equality relation applies to JSON guard values, including numerically equivalent representations such as 1 and 1.0 and compound enum values?
What equality relation is used for guard values, especially for JSON numbers such as 1 and 1.0 and for arrays or objects?

judgement.why: This is the same guard-value equality question already answered by the later run contract in P50.

precedent.topic: Exact equality semantics for guard values
quotes: advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract defines guard equality as equality of canonical JSON text.

topics.topic: Meaning of an earlier implementation for rollback eligibility
questions: What exactly makes an implementation “earlier,” especially after a rollback: submission order, activation order, or merely being a non-current existing implementation?
Does "earlier" require an implementation to predate the current implementation or to have been active before, and may rollback select a later admitted implementation after a previous rollback?

judgement.why: This is the same rollback-eligibility question already answered by the later function contract in P12.

precedent.topic: Eligibility requirements for selecting a rollback implementation
quotes: roll_back_slot: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises UnknownReferenceError for an unknown slot, then for an unknown implementation; then RefusedError when the implementation belongs to a contract version other than the slot's current one, and RefusedError when it holds no admitted verdict over the current corpus digest; it runs no admission.

roll_back_slot: [BEHAVIOR] Naming the implementation that is already the current activation returns that Activation and records nothing; otherwise one RecordActivationChange is written through record_change with activated_at from kernel_now and the given actor.
precedent.why: The later function contract permits any existing implementation of the current contract version with a current-corpus admitted verdict; the current implementation is merely a no-op case.

topics.topic: Required and permitted port-key sets in authored trial cases
questions: Must authored trial inputs contain every and only input port, and must expected outputs, when present, contain every and only output port?
Must authored `inputs` contain exactly every input port and no extra names, and, when `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every output port and no extras?

judgement.why: This is the same authored trial-case port-completeness question already assigned to State 6 in P6.

precedent.topic: Exact input and expected-output port completeness for trial cases
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Start and end events included in the sandbox wall-time deadline
questions: At what event does `wall_time_ms` begin and end: environment creation, interpreter start, module loading, entry to `run`, return from `run`, or completed cleanup?
Does `wall_time_ms` include sandbox creation, input staging, module loading, output validation and cleanup, or only the call to `run`?

quotes:
ResourceBounds M04 are enforced from outside the environment with `setrlimit`
   (address space, processes) and the parent's own wall deadline and output
   count.
judgement.why: The events starting and ending the wall-time interval were already unspecified by this unchanged passage, and the change did not make that choice newly material.

topics.topic: Tie-breaking order for distinct edges or constants with identical stated sort keys
questions: How are edges or constants ordered for hashing when their stated sort keys are equal but their remaining content differs?
If two distinct edges have the same four endpoint fields, what orders them when their guards differ and one fails before the other?
When two distinct edges have the same four endpoint fields, in which deterministic order are their guard, cardinality, disclosure and failure checks performed?
How are distinct constants with the same target ordered for identity hashing and deterministic failure reporting?

judgement.why: This is the same tie-breaking question for duplicate-looking flow edges and constants already judged in P44, and the relevant ordering text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Canonical ordering of duplicate-looking flow edges and constants for hashing and failure selection
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Unit used for disclosed failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed failure-detail length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes, or the original untruncated text?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?

judgement.why: This is the same failure-detail length-unit question already answered by the later surface note in P28.

precedent.topic: Length unit disclosed for redacted failure details
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Validation of binding schemas against the supported JSON Schema subset
questions: Must every binding input and output schema be validated against the same supported JSON Schema subset before proposal is kept?
Must every binding input and output schema be accepted by the kernel's supported JSON Schema subset, and where does that check occur in proposal and acceptance order?

judgement.why: This is the same supported-schema enforcement question for binding and flow ports already answered by the State 6 text in P37.

precedent.topic: Supported-schema enforcement for non-contract ports and constants
quotes:
a
   schema is a JSON object using only `type` (one of `null`, `boolean`,
   `integer`, `number`, `string`, `array`, `object`, as one string), `enum`
   (a non-empty array of distinct scalars), `const` (one scalar), `properties`
   and `required` (for `object`), `additionalProperties` (`true` or `false`
   only), `items` (one schema, for `array`), `minItems`, `maxItems`,
   `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minimum` and `maximum`. Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.

A flow constant is a typed literal
   (M16): the composing agent declares its `value_schema` with its class, and its
   StoredValue takes both. Composition refuses a constant whose value does not
   fit its declared schema (A05 rule 7); phase 2 of the proof checks that the
   declared schema is the target port's stored schema (M21), so the value then
   fits the port (A05 rule 1); the constant's identity does not depend on
   resolving another record.
precedent.why: State 6 defines the supported subset, makes unsupported binding or flow-port schemas accept no value, and therefore makes a constant under such a schema fail composition's value-fit check.

topics.topic: Validity and reuse of admission verdicts across executions and release upgrades
questions: Is admission validity defined permanently by the first verdict, or must the implementation be demonstrably deterministic before cached verdicts are authoritative?

After installing a new release, may existing AdmissionVerdicts be reused and may unfinished runs execute their pinned implementations under the new sandbox runtime, or must the old runtime remain available or evidence be regenerated?

quotes:
Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
   admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
   current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.
judgement.why: Whether cached verdicts and pinned implementations survive a release change was already unspecified around this unchanged reuse rule, and the change did not make that question newly material.

topics.topic: Whether encoded or coincidental credential data must be withheld from responses
questions: May a service response containing an encoded form of a credential be returned as an `open` or `business_confidential` value, despite State 0 saying secrets never enter an answer?

Does this prohibit only serialization of configured authentication fields, or must every response be scanned and withheld when ordinary user or service data contains bytes equal to an owner or agent token?

quotes:
Secrets — service credentials and tokens live in the installation's
   protected configuration; they never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an
   answer.

A service's own answer is not the
   kernel's text: a body that echoes the value verbatim, 2xx or not, is
   withheld and never used as an output (A09 rule 7); one that carries it in
   another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: State 0 says credentials and tokens never enter an answer, while A17 permits an encoded credential to pass through subject only to its disclosure class.
judgement.failure: a contradiction needs two quotes found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Atomic visibility of mapped outputs when one output exceeds its ceiling
questions: If one mapped output list is within the ceiling and another is over it, are any valid lists delivered or exposed as run outputs before the node is treated as failed?

topics.topic: Authoritative bytes and digest during configuration hot reload
questions: If the file changes between the digest read and the parsing read, which bytes are authoritative and what digest is remembered?

topics.topic: Canonical hexadecimal case for percent encoding across URL components
questions: Must percent escapes use uppercase or lowercase hexadecimal digits, and is the same rule used for path placeholders and query names and values?

topics.topic: Checks repeated during stale-manifest pre-send validation
questions: Does pre-send validation repeat idempotency-key-to-binding-port and request-shape compatibility checks, or only parse and validate the manifest capability entry before comparing its digest?

topics.topic: Crash-safe atomic publication of files and referencing database records
questions: Across a crash, how is it guaranteed that no committed record names a missing file while allowing only harmless unreferenced published files?

topics.topic: Default size and pagination controls for the repair evidence window
questions: How many NodeExecutions does the repair view return by default, and can the caller page or choose the count?

topics.topic: Element state after an unknown attempt is resolved as not_applied
questions: After resolving an unknown attempt as `not_applied`, is the element concluded as failed or does it remain unconcluded and waiting for a fresh approval?

topics.topic: Encoding used for token acceptance, length measurement, and constant-time comparison
questions: Are non-ASCII token strings accepted, and over which byte representation is length and constant-time equality measured?

topics.topic: Event at which an approval is considered consumed
questions: Is an approval considered used by committing the in-flight attempt or only after the first request byte is written?

topics.topic: Exact representation returned by the clock module for persisted timestamps
questions: What exact value does the clock module return for persisted timestamps?

topics.topic: Exact set of actions exposed as MCP operations
questions: Which actions actually exist as MCP operations?

topics.topic: Failure location reported for fan-in errors caused by multiple edges
questions: When several deliverable edges cause one fan-in failure, which edge or pair is named in ProofResult, or may the failure name only the target port?

topics.topic: Handling cryptographic hash collisions in identities and content-addressed storage
questions: What happens if different meaning facts produce an already-existing SHA-256 identity?
What happens when different byte sequences have the same digest and size?

topics.topic: How design_lint establishes completeness of security-review categories
questions: How can `design_lint` determine that the listed security categories are complete rather than merely that each listed category is well formed?

topics.topic: How reachability propagates from a node input to its outputs
questions: When reachability enters a node through one input, does every output of that node count as reachable, or only outputs with an explicitly defined dependency on that input?

topics.topic: Number of clock readings used in one multi-fact store change
questions: How many wall-clock readings are taken for a change that writes multiple timestamped facts?

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when cleanup fails after another execution failure
questions: If an execution first times out or exhausts a resource and cleanup then cannot be confirmed, is its recorded outcome the earlier outcome or `crashed/cleanup_failed`?

topics.topic: Policy for wall-clock regression between persisted records
questions: May a later record have an earlier timestamp, or must the clock module clamp or refuse regressing time?

topics.topic: Precedence among multiple endpoint-condition failures on one edge
questions: When several endpoint conditions fail on one edge, what exact source-versus-target and existence-versus-direction order determines the reported first reason?

topics.topic: Scope of digest replacement in a personal-data approval preview
questions: Does “only the request's digest” replace just the built-request field, or the entire preview including operation metadata and non-personal inputs?

topics.topic: Scope of trace as the sole source for continuation state and authority
questions: Does "trace" include all run-related authority and attempt records, or is the sole-source claim limited to execution history?

topics.topic: Scratch accounting and outcome when sandbox setup exceeds the scratch ceiling
questions: What bytes count toward scratch usage, and what record and outcome result when setup itself exceeds the scratch ceiling?

topics.topic: Size calculation and outcome for non-canonically encodable return values
questions: How is output size computed, and which outcome is selected, when a returned value cannot be canonically encoded?

topics.topic: TrialCase representation of a failed mapped element for a many-cardinality input
questions: When a failed mapped execution received one element in place of a contract port whose cardinality is `many`, what becomes the TrialCase input so that it fits the contract port?

topics.topic: Valid JSON shape of exposed_as.http_api and single versus multiple routes
questions: Which JSON representations of `exposed_as` and `http_api` are valid, and how is one route distinguished from several?

topics.topic: Validation behavior when resubmitting an old contract after ceilings decrease
questions: If an author resubmits an existing old contract whose bounds exceed the current release ceilings, is the existing record returned or is the request refused by current validation?

topics.topic: Validation that an activated version belongs to the named flow
questions: Must an activation request name both a flow and one of its own versions, and what happens if it names a version belonging to another flow?

topics.topic: Where a run pins the exact FlowActivation identity
questions: Where is the exact FlowActivation identity pinned so a later draft-write attempt can name it unambiguously after restarts and reactivations?

topics.topic: Where caller-supplied content-derived identities are forbidden or required
questions: For which creation operations and fields is supplying a content-derived identity forbidden, and where is it required as an existing-record reference?

topics.topic: Whether bounded_text_bytes_max applies to strings nested inside stored values
questions: Does `bounded_text_bytes_max` also limit strings nested inside a value already governed by `stored_value_bytes_max`?

topics.topic: Whether deterministic seeded pseudorandomness is permitted
questions: Does State 0 prohibit all random-number APIs, including deterministic seeded pseudorandom generation, or only access to nondeterministic entropy?

topics.topic: Whether path-placeholder ports must have cardinality one
questions: Must a path-placeholder input port also have cardinality `one`, or may a binding be accepted although every invocation with that `many` port will fail pre-send?

topics.topic: Whether the service-response byte ceiling is aggregate or separately applied
questions: Is `service_response_bytes_max` one limit for the entire response or two independent limits, one for status-plus-headers and another for the body?
